summary: Tested all 4 forms (curriculum/specimen/quiet-list magnets + apply drawer) and 2 PDF endpoints end-to-end. Backend 14/14 pytest pass. Frontend critical flows all wire to /api/* and return 200; previously-working interactions (tabs, reveal, deliverables, countdown, marquee) intact.

integration_issues.issue: When an invalid email is typed, the browser's native HTML5 type=email blocks form submit, so the inline [data-testid=leadmagnet-*-error] never appears. The test request 'Invalid email in any magnet shows an inline error' is satisfied only by the browser bubble, not by an in-page styled error. Consider adding a regex pre-check in submit() to render the styled inline error to match the design language.

action_items: (Optional / cosmetic) Add a lightweight client-side email-regex check inside useMagnetForm.submit so the styled inline error appears instead of (or in addition to) the browser's native validation bubble.

(Optional naming nit) Section testid is 'leadmagnet-quietlist' but the input/submit/success/error use the prefix 'leadmagnet-quiet-'. Curriculum and Specimen are consistent (all 'leadmagnet-curriculum-*'). Consider standardising the quiet-list prefix for clarity.

rca of the issue:
No blocking bugs found. The only spec deviation is that 'inline error on invalid email' relies on HTML5 native validation rather than the styled

. Root cause: useMagnetForm.submit() only sets `err` from server responses (try/catch around axios.post); since HTML5 'required + type=email' aborts submit before fetch, setErr is never called. Fix: in submit(), before axios.post, run a regex check on email and call setErr('Please enter a valid email address.') + return early if invalid.
